html:
Marc Chagall was a painter, born in 1887 near Vitebsk in today's Belarus to a Hasidic Jewish family, whose dreamlike pictures of village life made him one of the best known modern artists.

He grew up in the Pale of Settlement, studied in Saint Petersburg and lived in Paris before World War I. After the Russian Revolution he founded an art school in Vitebsk in 1918, where Kazimir Malevich also taught. He left for good in 1922. In France and America he painted floating lovers, fiddlers and goats, and later stained glass and the ceiling of the Paris Opera. He escaped Nazi occupied France in 1941. The Vitebsk of his youth, destroyed in the war, lives on mainly in his work.
